display.purpose: Homepage hero h1 only. Used once per page at most. Tight leading collapses multiple lines into a single visual block.

headline.purpose: Section headings across all pages. Carries colour emphasis via italic <em> in Signal Pink or Worn Sage.

title.purpose: Card headings and sub-headings. Lora at a working scale — editorial but not monumental.

body.purpose: All prose copy. 17px for UI copy; 20–22px italic Lora for section-opening intro paragraphs. Max 65ch.

label.purpose: Category badges, section eyebrows, stat chips, progress percentages. Always uppercase, always tracked.

handwrite.purpose: Decorative annotations only — sticky notes, margin callouts, captions. Never used for interactive or functional text.

shadows.name: card-ambient
shadows.purpose: Post cards and content cards at rest. Two-layer warm shadow.

shadows.name: surface-float
shadows.purpose: Larger containers (checklist card, workshop section) on coloured backgrounds.

shadows.name: note-pin
shadows.purpose: Sticky notes, washi-tape pinned elements. Compact — for physically-attached small objects.

shadows.name: photo-dramatic
shadows.purpose: Polaroid photo frame only. Heavy ambient shadow suggests a photograph lifted off a table.

shadows.name: btn-hover-glow
shadows.purpose: Primary and subscribe button hover state. Studio Plum tint — reads as a warm coloured aura.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for all state transitions (button hover, link colour, nav underline).

motion.name: ease-reveal
motion.purpose: Section reveal: translateY(28px) + opacity fade-in on scroll entry.

motion.name: ease-handwrite
motion.purpose: Caveat annotation clip-path reveal. Mimics the pace of handwriting.

motion.name: ease-draw-svg
motion.purpose: SVG path stroke-dashoffset draw. Slightly snappier than handwrite.

motion.name: ease-card-lift
motion.purpose: Card hover: translateY(-6px) + rotation-to-0deg + shadow deepen.

components.name: Handwrite Annotation
components.description: Caveat text that reveals via clip-path as if being written in real time. Always aria-hidden, always rotated, always protruding beyond its parent.
components.html: ← my favourite this month ♡
components.css: .ds-annotation { font-family: 'Caveat', cursive; font-size: 22px; font-weight: 600; color: #C9347E; line-height: 1.35; clip-path: inset(0 100% -12% 0); -webkit-clip-path: inset(0 100% -12% 0); transition: clip-path 1.3s cubic-bezier(0.45,0.1,0.35,1), -webkit-clip-path 1.3s cubic-bezier(0.45,0.1,0.35,1); position: absolute; z-index: 10; pointer-events: none; } .ds-annotation.written { clip-path: inset(0 0% -12% 0); -webkit-clip-path: inset(0 0% -12% 0); } .ds-annotation--fast { transition-duration: 0.9s; } .ds-annotation--slow { transition-duration: 1.9s; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-annotation { clip-path: none !important; -webkit-clip-path: none !important; } }

narrative.overview:
Handmade Logic looks and feels like a beloved, well-used sketchbook: layered surfaces, colour tests at the edges, annotations in the margins, nothing too precious. The visual system carries the same honesty as the writing — imperfection is not a flaw to correct, it is the character to preserve. A slight rotation on a card, a handwritten note pointing at something, a watercolour wash that bleeds just past its container: these are features, not bugs.

The palette is warm and saturated but never slick. Signal Pink, Golden Hour, and Worn Sage sit on a cream ground that reads like unbleached paper rather than a web background. Every shadow is tinted toward Ink Plum, never cool grey.

Typography is the workhorse. Lora carries the editorial weight; Nunito handles the UI without fuss; Caveat appears only where a real pen might. Motion is purposeful and unhurried.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, imperfect, annotated — a working notebook, not a portfolio
Layered surfaces: dotted canvas background, watercolour washes, slight element rotations
Three-tier typography: Lora for authority, Nunito for clarity, Caveat strictly for personality
All shadows tinted with Ink Plum — never cool grey
Cards rest at slight angles; they straighten and lift on hover
Handwriting annotations reveal via clip-path sweep, as if written in real time

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: All shadows use rgba(42,24,37,...) — Ink Plum, not grey. A grey shadow on this palette reads as cold and disconnected. Prohibited.

rules.name: The No Pure Neutral Rule
rules.body: No #000, no #fff, no rgba(0,0,0,...). Every neutral is tinted toward the raspberry/plum hue family at low chroma.

rules.name: The Signal Pink Reserve Rule
rules.body: Signal Pink is used on 10–20% of any given screen surface. Its rarity is the point. Reach for Golden Hour for warmth without urgency; Studio Plum for weight without competition.

rules.name: The Caveat Fence Rule
rules.body: Caveat appears in annotations, captions, and asides — never as primary text for any interactive element. If an interaction relies on Caveat to communicate, that text belongs in Lora or Nunito.

rules.name: The Italic Em Rule
rules.body: Within Lora headings, key words are wrapped in <em> and coloured Signal Pink or Worn Sage. This is the heading emphasis system — not bold, not underline, not size increase.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: Shadows respond to state, not decoration. A surface at rest carries only enough shadow to separate it from the layer below. Decorative heavy shadows at rest are prohibited.

rules.name: The Warm Tint Rule
rules.body: No shadow uses neutral grey (rgba(0,0,0,...)). All shadows carry Ink Plum (rgba(42,24,37,...)). A grey shadow is a sign something escaped the system.

dos: Do use Ink Plum shadows (rgba(42,24,37,...)) for every drop shadow.
Do rotate cards and placed elements by 1–3° at rest.
Do restrict Caveat to annotations, captions, and aside text.
Do reserve Signal Pink for primary actions and heading emphasis.
Do open every major section with the badge pattern: Golden Hour pill + Nunito bold label + small SVG icon.
Do mark every Caveat annotation aria-hidden="true".
Do tint every neutral toward the Ink Plum/raspberry family at low chroma.
donts: Don't build a minimal tech aesthetic: no dark mode, no monospace body type, no developer-cool visual language.
Don't build a slick, corporate lifestyle surface: no polished wellness gradients, no DTC craft-brand photography, no flatlay beige-and-white minimalism.
Don't use maximalist competing elements — every decorative element earns its place.
Don't use Pinterest softness, Etsy flatlay minimalism, or stock-photo warmth.
Don't use border-left greater than 1px as a coloured accent stripe.
Don't build identical card grids — vary column widths, rotation angles, and image heights.
Don't animate with bounce or elastic easing.
Don't use em dashes in UI copy.
Don't use Caveat for interactive or functional text.
